title: Customer Acceptance Test Suite and SLA Matrix for Private Deployments
author: Elena Voss
body:
Overview:
This document defines a reproducible Customer Acceptance Test (CAT) suite and a companion SLA matrix that should be run and agreed during onboarding for Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on-prem). The goal is to provide a clear, executable set of tests and pass/fail thresholds that establish a baseline for go-live and ongoing SLO verification.

Intended audience:
- Customer Success (onboarding leads)
- Solutions Engineering
- Customer platform and networking teams
- Deployment and SRE engineers

Scope:
- Applies to private-control-plane + data-plane deployments (VPC and on-prem installers) where Redwood runtime will be used to serve inference workloads.
- Covers networking, security, performance (latency/throughput), persistence, observability, upgrade/rollback, and failover behavior.

Glossary (short):
- CAT: Customer Acceptance Test
- SLO: Service Level Objective
- KV-cache: key-value attention cache used by the serving runtime
- Control plane: Redwood-managed control components (can be hybrid)
- Data plane: customer-hosted runtime components

Executive acceptance criteria (summary):
1) All critical CAT items (networking, auth, and basic correctness) must pass in the customer environment.
2) Performance tests must meet the thresholds in the SLA matrix below for 95th and 99th latency percentiles under the agreed load profile.
3) Observability: traces, per-request logs, and token-level cost metrics are visible in the console/forwarded telemetry.
4) Upgrade & rollback: a staged upgrade completes without data loss and can be reverted within the rollback window.

CAT structure and test IDs:
- Each test has a stable ID: CAT-{area}-{number} (e.g. CAT-NET-01).
- Tests are grouped by area: NETWORK, AUTH, PERF, FAILOVER, OBS, UPGRADE.

1) NETWORKING

CAT-NET-01: Control plane connectivity check- Description: Verify runtime nodes can reach Redwood control endpoints necessary for heartbeats, model fetch, and metrics export.- Preconditions: TLS certs and firewall rules applied per network plan.- Steps:
  1. From each runtime host, run: curl -v https://control.redwood.example.com/healthz (use customer-resolved endpoint).
  2. Check TCP connectivity on ports 443 and 5222 (if using realtime).
- Expected result: 200 OK and TLS handshake completes. Latency < 150ms for control API calls from data-plane to control-plane in same region.

CAT-NET-02: Egress and proxy path validation- Description: Ensure egress/proxy rules do not break streaming or long-lived connections.
- Steps:
  1. Simulate a 30s streaming generation via curl or the SDK with chunked responses.
  2. Assert no reset/FIN observed.
- Expected result: Stream completes and chunks arrive within 500ms of token emission on average.

2) AUTH & KEY MANAGEMENT

CAT-AUTH-01: KMS integration and key rotation test- Description: Validate that model artifacts and secrets are encrypted with the customer KMS and that rotating keys does not break runtime.
- Steps:
  1. Encrypt a test secret via the configured KMS key and start the runtime.
  2. Trigger key rotation (per customer KMS process).
  3. Restart affected services.
- Expected: Services start and continue to decrypt previously-encrypted artifacts. No data loss.

CAT-AUTH-02: RBAC and token scope enforcement- Description: Confirm per-route API keys and RBAC entries prevent unauthorized model access.
- Steps:
  1. Create a scoped API token limited to embeddings. Try a generation call; expect 403.
  2. Create a full-scope token and ensure successful call.
- Expected: 403 for scoped token when calling forbidden endpoints; 200 for allowed operations.

3) PERFORMANCE (PERF)

Notes on load profiles:
- Define a Customer Load Profile (CLP) before tests. Example CLP-BURST: 100 RPS sustained for 5m, 500 RPS bursts for 1m.
- Tests must be run from load generators located in same AZ/region as runtime to avoid cross-region noise.

CAT-PERF-01: Baseline p95/p99 latency test (tokenized generation)- Description: Measure p95/p99 latency per request at the CLP baseline. Use real model + prompt set provided in Appendix A.
- Steps:
  1. Warm runtime with 300 sample requests to prime KV cache.
  2. Run the load generator (wrk or locust) for 10 minutes at the agreed RPS.
  3. Collect per-request latencies and distribution.
- Expected (SLA thresholds):
  - p95 end-to-end latency <= 220ms for short seq (512 tokens)
  - p99 end-to-end latency <= 420ms for short seq (512 tokens)
  - Throughput target: sustained RPS within 10% of the CLP baseline

CAT-PERF-02: Cold-start latency with model pull- Description: Boot fresh runtime nodes and measure time to first successful inference while model artifact is being pulled.
- Expected: Model pull + first inference <= 90s for a 6GB quantized model via optimized image registry within the LAN.

4) FAILOVER & RESILIENCE

CAT-FAIL-01: Node termination graceful draining- Description: Terminate one runtime process/disrupt container and verify in-flight requests are drained and not dropped.
- Steps:
  1. Start 30 concurrent requests that run for ~10s.
  2. Send SIGTERM to a runtime worker or cordon a node in Kubernetes.
- Expected: In-flight requests complete; new requests are routed to healthy nodes. Error rate < 1% during event.

CAT-FAIL-02: Zone outage simulation- Description: Simulate AZ failure and validate multi-zone traffic shifting.
- Preconditions: Multi-zone deployment per reference architecture required.
- Expected: Route shift completed within 45s; p99 increase < 2x baseline; no model consistency issues.

5) OBSERVABILITY (OBS)

CAT-OBS-01: Token-level cost and trace visibility- Description: Ensure console shows token-level accounting and request traces with model/version tags for sampled requests.
- Steps:
  1. Generate 20 sample requests with unique trace IDs.
  2. Verify traces appear in console and are correlated with metric events.
- Expected: All traces available within 60s of request completion.

CAT-OBS-02: Alerting pipeline smoke test- Description: Trigger a synthetic high-error-rate (>= 5% for 2m) and validate alerts fire to the configured pager/Slack channel.
- Steps:
  1. Use the test harness to inject error responses at 6% for 3 minutes.
  2. Confirm alerting pipeline (Prometheus -> Alertmanager -> PagerDuty/Slack) sends notification within 3 minutes.
- Expected: Alert received by oncall and recorded in the incident log.

6) UPGRADE & ROLLBACK

CAT-UGRD-01: Staged canary upgrade- Description: Perform a canary upgrade of runtime from version A -> B following rollout policy (5% canary, 10m observation).
- Steps:
  1. Deploy new image to 5% of nodes. Monitor error/latency metrics for 10 minutes.
  2. If no regressions, increase to 25%, then 100% per policy. If regressions, trigger rollback.
- Expected: No behavioral regressions for key prompts; upgrade time per node < 5 minutes for pulling and restarting.

CAT-UGRD-02: Rollback validation- Description: Validate rollback completes and that previously-serving model versions continue to respond correctly.
- Steps:
  1. Simulate a failed canary with increased error rates.
  2. Execute rollback and confirm 100% of traffic served by the previous version within 5 minutes.
- Expected: All endpoints respond within normal latency windows; no data loss.

Acceptance thresholds and SLA matrix (example):

| Area        | Metric                       | Target (SLA)                         | Measurement window |
|-------------|------------------------------|--------------------------------------|--------------------|
| Latency     | p95 request (short seq)      | <= 220ms                             | 10m                |
| Latency     | p99 request (short seq)      | <= 420ms                             | 10m                |
| Availability| Successful requests (slo)    | >= 99.95%                            | 30d                |
| Recovery    | Node replacement recovery    | <= 120s for routing to healthy node  | per-event          |
| Observability| Trace visibility lag        | <= 60s                                | 10m                |
| Upgrade     | Canary rollback time         | <= 5m to full rollback               | per-event          |

Note: SLA values above are baseline examples. Final SLA matrix must be mutually agreed and signed in the onboarding contract.

Artifacts required from customer for CAT:
- Network diagram and firewall/security group rules.
- KMS key ARN and rotation policy document.
- Test VPC/subnet where load generators will run (must be in same AZ).
- Service account/credentials for registry access (if models are in customer registry).
- Representative prompt set and test dataset (Appendix A).

Redwood responsibilities during CAT:
- Provide CAT runner scripts and load generator images.
- Provide access to a signed test image and deployment manifests for installer.
- Observe and advise on tuning (batching, worker count, kernel selection) during runs.

Customer responsibilities during CAT:
- Provide requested network and credentials artifacts before test window.
- Nominate 1-2 engineers as points-of-contact for the test window.
- Reserve time for a 2-hour remediation window post-CAT to address any configuration gaps.

Onboarding execution plan (step-by-step):
1. Pre-test readiness (2 business days prior)
   - Exchange artifacts (network diagram, KMS docs, credentials).
   - Agree CLP and test window.
   - Deployment smoke: basic install and health-checks (CAT-NET-01, CAT-AUTH-01).
2. Baseline runs (Day 0)
   - Warm the runtime and run CAT-PERF-01 for baseline.
   - Run OBS checks (CAT-OBS-01) concurrently.
3. Stress & resilience (Day 1)
   - Run failover tests (CAT-FAIL-01, CAT-FAIL-02).
   - Run upgrade dry-run (CAT-UGRD-01 on a canary subset).
4. Acceptance review (Day 1 afternoon)
   - Consolidate results into acceptance report template.
   - If all critical items pass, issue acceptance sign-off; otherwise, list remediation items and schedule re-run.

Sample commands and snippets:
- Control plane health check:
  curl -v --header "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN" https://control.redwood.example.com/healthz

- Simple load test with wrk2 (example):
  wrk -t8 -c200 -d600s -R100 --latency --timeout 30s --script=redwood-wrk-lua.lua https://runtime.internal.redwood.example.com/v1/generate

- Example SLO rule (Prometheus recording style):
  """
  - record: runtime:request_latency_ms:p95
    expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[10m])) by (le))
  """

Appendix A: Minimal prompt set for performance profiling:
- 50 short prompts (~20 tokens output) representing user-facing responses.
- 20 medium prompts (~200 tokens output) representing document summarization.
- 10 long prompts (~1000 tokens output) for stress tests (run at low concurrency).

Acceptance report template (deliverables):
- Test run artifacts (load generator logs, per-request traces, aggregated latency histograms).
- Pass/fail matrix for all CAT-* tests.
- Observed SLA metrics and any deviations annotated with root cause.
- Remediation plan with owners and target dates (if any failures).

Escalation & signoff process:
1. If test failures are blocking, CSC/SE opens an onboarding ticket and tags escalation@redwood.com.
2. Within 2 business hours an oncall engineer will be assigned.
3. Customer signoff: 2 authorized customer approvers must sign the acceptance report.

Maintenance: periodic revalidation
- Recommendation: run a smoke CAT suite weekly and full PERF/FAIL suite quarterly or before any major change (e.g., model variant, runtime version, KMS rotation).

Document ownership and change log:
- Owner: Customer Success (Elena Voss)
- Review cadence: Quarterly or on major product/references changes.
- Change log:
  - 2026-01-10: Created initial CAT & SLA matrix (Elena Voss).
  - 2026-02-14: Added canary upgrade and rollback timing guidance; tightened default latency thresholds (reviewers: Marco Liu, Priya Shah).

Contact and support
- Onboarding lead: elena.voss@redwood.com
- Escalation contact: escalation@redwood.com (for high priority onboarding failures)

End of document.
